verdict.rationale: SES documents SNS notifications for bounced, complained, and delivered events (amazon-ses-docs-23) and broader event publishing to SNS/EventBridge/CloudWatch via configuration sets (amazon-ses-docs-10, amazon-ses-docs-28, amazon-ses-docs-38, amazon-ses-docs-29), which can be wired to HTTP endpoints to act as webhooks. However, this is SNS/EventBridge pub-sub, not a native 'webhook' primitive, and no evidence documents retry/backoff semantics for failed webhook deliveries. Community notes SES logging is thin, requiring developers to maintain their own logs (amazon-ses-comm-1). Missing for 10: explicit documented retry/backoff policy for event delivery, native webhook endpoint configuration (vs. requiring SNS/Lambda glue), and independent confirmation of delivery guarantees.
